newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela blames Denko for Venalum row.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela blames Denko for Venalum row.

text.p: Venezuela has blamed Japanese firm Showa Denko for blocking negotiations aimed at settling a long-running dispute over veto rights at the Venalum aluminum smelter, said state holding company Corporacion de Venezolana de Guayana (CVG).

"Showa Denko has persisted in its desire to maintain a privileged position within Venalum...so blocking the Venezuelan government's aluminum industry privatization program," CVG president Elias Ynaty said in press statement datelined Tokyo.
"Its position is particularly difficult to understand as two other Japanese firms in the CVG-Venalum group have expressed interest in participating in its privatization," Ynaty added.

Other Japanese investors in the Venalum smelter consortium include Kobe Steel Ltd, Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Materials Corp, Mitsubishi Aluminum Co Ltd and Marubeni Corp. Venalum's privatization, slated for later this year, has run aground in disputes over the Japanese consortium's 20 percent preferential share of the company that grants veto rights.
Ynaty did not say privatization of the smelter would not go ahead. But the statement apparently hardens Venezuela's earlier position.
Venezuela Investment Fund (FIV) President Alberto Poletto said on Wednesday morning the Japanese consortium would be willing to accept some changes, but "it depends on some compromise on our side."
Ynaty and Poletto are due to leave for South Korea on Thursday morning, leaving behind a technical team to continue talks in Japan until Friday.
